doc.title: Kristen Korb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000

title: Learning the business end
summary: Holly Hofmann helps with business; Korb is self-sufficient and learns the hard way.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Did you get to learn the business end of things a little bit also then?

Holly. Holly has been really good about that. And I’ve been one that I’ve always been pretty self-sufficient. And I know that in order to get to where I need to be I have to take care of business. Because nobody else is going to do it for me. And you really don’t have anybody else to lean on. So it’s been one of those things that — I’ve been pleased — I

mean you take your knocks along the way and you learn stuff the hard way, but at the same time I like, we have to, we just, there’s no other way about it. It’s like sink or swim. And if you don’t take care of business it’s going to bite you.
